Sign in, view and find resources, view resource details, submit booking requests, view own bookings/requests, and cancel an eligible own booking
Lab Staff ( Lab managers or operational laboratory staff when reporting operational/data issues ):
Sign in and report resource problems or data-correction issues so that an authorised administrator can review and resolve them

G-0: Maintain accurate and traceable lab data in one central system.

The lab currently keeps operational data in separate tools and manual records, which can lead to inconsistent, duplicated, or difficult-to-audit information. This iteration centralises resource management, booking, issue reporting, role-based access, authentication, administrative records, and change history for the three system actors defined above.

Reports and data export, budgeting, integrations with external operational systems, and production deployment infrastructure are outside the scope of this iteration. Docker containerisation is included only to provide a consistent development/testing runtime and deployment packaging basis.
SG-1 - Achieve: Provide lab members with resource visibility and reliable booking.
Rationale: Lab members need to know which resources exist and reserve them without clashing with other members' approved usage.
SG-2 - Maintain: Accurate and consistent lab records.
Rationale: Resource, booking, issue-report, and operational data should follow consistent formats to reduce duplicate, missing, or incorrect information.
SG-3 - Achieve: Allow authorised users to manage lab data.
Rationale: Administrative data-management actions should remain restricted to authorised administrators while normal users receive only the functions required by their role.
SG-4 - Avoid: Unauthorised or accidental modification of lab data.
Rationale: Google OAuth 2.0 authentication and role-based access control protect restricted functions and data from unauthorised modification.
SG-5 - Maintain: Traceable and auditable lab records.
Rationale: Important changes should record the acting user, timestamp, action, and affected record so that administrators can review what changed and when.
As a lab member, I want to view lab resources so that I can know what resources are available for use.
The system displays current non-archived resources.
As a lab member, I want to find lab resources so that I can quickly narrow and organise the resource list.
The resource list supports search by name, filtering by category and availability status, and sorting by name, category, or availability status.
As a lab member, I want to view resource details so that I can decide whether a resource is suitable for my work.
The selected resource shows description, location, responsible person, availability, and current status.
As a lab member, I want to submit a booking request so that I can use a resource during a required time period.
A booking request is created only when the required booking data is valid and the resource is available for the requested period.
As a lab member, I want to view my bookings and requests so that I can track my planned resource usage.
The system shows only the lab member's own bookings and requests with their current status.
As a lab member, I want to cancel my booking so that I can release a time period I no longer need.
A lab member can cancel only their own booking before its start time, and the reserved period is released.
As a lab staff member, I want to report a resource problem so that the administrator can correct the central record or arrange maintenance.
The report stores the affected resource, problem type, description, reporter, submission time, and Pending status, and the administrator is notified.
As a system administrator, I want to create a resource record so that a new lab resource can be managed in the system.
An authorised administrator can create a valid resource record.
As a system administrator, I want to edit a resource record so that lab information remains accurate.
An authorised administrator can save valid changes to an existing resource record.
As a system administrator, I want to archive a resource record so that retired resources are hidden from normal lab-member views.
An authorised administrator can archive a resource; archived resources remain visible in the administrator view but not in the normal member list.
As a system administrator, I want to set resource availability so that members can see whether a resource can currently be booked.
An authorised administrator can change the availability status of a resource.
As a system administrator, I want to review a pending booking request so that I can approve valid requests or reject unsuitable ones.
The administrator can approve or reject a pending request; approval reserves the requested period, rejection records a reason, and the requester is notified of the decision.
As a system administrator, I want to resolve an issue report so that the reported resource problem has a recorded outcome.
An authorised administrator can update the report status, add a resolution note, and notify the reporter.
As a system administrator, I want to manage a user role so that each user has permissions appropriate to their responsibilities.
An authorised administrator can assign or revoke a role, and the corresponding permissions take effect immediately after the change is saved.
As a system administrator, I want to view change history so that I can audit who changed what and when.
The history shows the acting user, affected record, action, and timestamp in chronological order.
As a user, I want to sign in using Google OAuth 2.0 so that I can securely access functions permitted by my role.
A user can sign in with Google OAuth 2.0; unauthenticated users cannot access protected functions.
As a system administrator, I want to view administrative records so that I can oversee laboratory operations from one place.
An authorised administrator can view resource, booking, issue-report, user-role, and audit-log records relevant to lab operations.
Lab members shall be able to browse current non-archived lab resources and find relevant resources using search, filtering, and sorting.
Lab members shall be able to view the details of a selected lab resource.
Lab members shall be able to submit a booking request for a specified time period, and the system shall prevent unavailable or conflicting bookings from being accepted.
Lab members shall be able to view their own bookings and requests and cancel an eligible own booking before its start time.
Lab staff shall be able to report a resource problem or data-correction issue.
An authorised administrator shall be able to manage resource records, including creating, editing, archiving, and setting availability.
An authorised administrator shall be able to review pending booking requests and approve or reject them.
An authorised administrator shall be able to resolve issue reports from lab staff.
An authorised administrator shall be able to manage user roles and permissions by assigning or revoking roles.
An authorised administrator shall be able to audit changes through a chronological history of resource, booking, issue-report, and role changes.
Users shall be able to securely sign in using Google OAuth 2.0 and access only functions permitted by their assigned role.
An authorised administrator shall be able to view administrative records for resources, bookings, issue reports, user roles, and audit logs.

The system shall display current non-archived resources to lab members and support search by resource name, filtering by category and availability status, and sorting by name, category, or availability status.
The system shall display the selected resource's description, location, responsible person, availability, and current status.

The system shall require a resource, start time, and end time for each booking request; reject the request when the resource is unavailable or overlaps an approved booking; and display the reason when the request is invalid.
The system shall save a valid booking request with the requester and an initial status of Pending.

The system shall show each lab member only their own bookings and requests with current status, allow cancellation before the booking start time, and release the reserved period when a booking is cancelled.

The system shall allow only an authorised administrator to review a pending booking request by approving or rejecting it; approval reserves the requested period and rejection stores the administrator's reason.
The system shall notify the booking requester when the status of their booking request changes.
The system shall require an affected resource, problem type, and description for each issue report; save the report with reporter, submission time, and Pending status; and notify the administrator.
The system shall allow only an authorised administrator to resolve an issue report by changing its status and adding a resolution note, and shall notify the reporter when the status changes.

The system shall allow only an authorised administrator to create, edit, archive, and set availability for resource records; reject records missing a valid name, category, or location; hide archived resources from normal member views; and keep archived records visible to administrators.
The system shall allow only an authorised administrator to assign or revoke a user role and shall apply the updated permissions immediately after the role change is saved.
The system shall authenticate users using Google OAuth 2.0 before protected functions are accessed and shall enforce permissions according to the authenticated user's assigned role.
The system shall record the acting user, timestamp, action, and affected record for changes to resource, booking, issue-report, and role records.
The system shall allow only an authorised administrator to view change history in chronological order.
The system shall allow only an authorised administrator to view administrative records for resources, bookings, issue reports, user roles, and audit logs.

The Lab Data Management System uses a Modular Monolithic Architecture with a Layered Client-Server structure. The system is implemented as a web application in which the frontend and backend are separated by an API interface, while backend modules operate within a single application and share a central MySQL database.

A modular monolith is suitable for the current scope because resource management, booking, issue reporting, role management, authentication, and audit logging are closely related but can still be separated into functional modules. This avoids the operational complexity of microservices while preserving clear responsibility boundaries and allowing individual modules to be changed without redesigning the entire system.

The React frontend is responsible for presentation and user interaction. The Node.js backend processes requests, validates input, enforces business rules and authorisation, coordinates functional modules, and communicates with the MySQL database. Google OAuth 2.0 authenticates users before protected functions are accessed; the backend then applies permissions from the user's assigned role.

Main communication flow: User -> React Frontend -> Node.js Backend -> Functional Module -> MySQL Database. Docker containers package the application runtime and dependencies so the development and testing environment can be reproduced consistently.

When a user performs an action through the React frontend, the request is sent to the Node.js backend. The backend authenticates the user when required, applies role-based authorisation, and delegates the request to the relevant functional module. Valid changes are stored in MySQL and auditable changes are also recorded in the audit log. Status changes that require user awareness trigger the corresponding booking or issue-report notification.

The selected data storage technology is MySQL, a Relational Database Management System (RDBMS), used as the primary persistent data store for the Lab Data Management System.

The data defined by the SRS is structured and relational. Core entities include users and roles, resources, booking requests, issue reports, and audit-log entries. These entities have explicit relationships and consistency rules: bookings reference a user and resource, issue reports reference an affected resource, and role assignments determine permissions available to authenticated users.

MySQL supports relational tables, primary and foreign keys, constraints, indexing, and transactional operations. Transactions help preserve consistency when booking decisions or cancellations are saved, resource availability is changed, issue reports are resolved, roles are updated, and audit records are written. Indexes also support the required search, filter, sort, and administrative retrieval operations.

Stores related records for users and roles, resources, bookings, issue reports, and audit logs. Keys and constraints maintain integrity; indexes support search, filtering, sorting, and record retrieval.

The recommended development environment is a local development machine with GitHub for version control/collaboration and Docker for a reproducible application runtime used during development and testing.

GitHub provides a central repository for source code, documentation, commits, and branches, allowing multiple team members to work on different parts of the system while retaining a traceable project history. Each team member develops and tests locally before synchronising changes through GitHub.

Docker provides a consistent runtime and dependency package across team members and provides the packaging basis for later deployment. Production deployment infrastructure remains outside the current iteration; Docker is included to standardise development/testing and deployment packaging.
Used to develop, run, and test resource management, booking, issue reporting, role management, authentication, and audit functionality.
Centralised source and documentation repository with commits, branches, reviews, and project history.
Team members work locally and synchronise changes through GitHub; branches and commits help reduce conflicts and track modifications.
Defines a reproducible application environment for development/testing and provides deployment packaging for the application runtime.
